name: Filippo Arena
bornNote: BORN AND BAPTISED THE SAME DAY at Scilla -- «infantem HODIE NATUM» -- and given the name PHILIPPUS NUNTIATUS. The extract was copied from the parish book of baptisms on 26 May 1815 for his own marriage file. It replaces the «c. 1794» this archive carried from his statement at his son's birth registration in 1819, where he gave his age as twenty-five; he was twenty-six.
source: Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186; Matrimoni 1851 atto 13; Nati 1861 atto 228; Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186 read in the processetti of 1851
note: Named in FOUR independent acts. The sea trade runs Orazio -> Filippo -> Francesco Antonio -> Rocco, four generations of sailors, and he was a MARINARO himself at twenty-two. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. HE WAS ALSO, FOR FIVE DAYS, THE ARCHIVE'S PUBLISHED WALL -- «his marriage to Domenica Costa is pre-civil, the Arena line stops here» -- because this archive believed Scilla's registers began in 1816. THEY BEGIN IN 1809. He married Domenica Costa on 12 NOVEMBER 1815, Matrimoni atto 29, and the act names his parents ORAZIO ARENA and LITTERIA MORABITO, both alive and both standing beside him, because at twenty-two he was still a minor under the code. Every negative reported for 1816 to 1819 was correct; the conclusion drawn from them was not. AND HE COULD WRITE: he signed his own marriage act «Filippo Arena sposo», and signed his son's birth act in 1819, in registers where almost nobody signs.

name: Domenica Costa
bornNote: BORN AND BAPTISED THE SAME DAY at Scilla, by the archpriest Giuseppe Ingigneri himself, and given the name DOMINICA JOSEPHA. This settles a five-year disagreement in this archive's favour of neither guess: she was twenty-eight at her marriage in November 1815, which fits exactly, and THIRTY-TWO -- not twenty-seven -- when her son Francesco Antonio was born in November 1819. The age in that birth act is five years wrong.
source: Scilla, Nati 1819, atto 186; Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186 read in the processetti of 1851
note: Filippo Arena's wife, and now one of the best-attested people in this archive: her baptism of 1787, her marriage of 1815, her son's birth in 1819. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. Her parents are GIOVANNI DE COSTA, dead at Scilla on 29 March 1790 when she was two, and MARTA ALFONZETTI, who was still alive to consent to the marriage twenty-five years later. NOTE THE SURNAME: Costa is also what her great-grandson Rocco married, in Generosa Costa, and a Lorenzo Costa was lodging with Rocco in New York in 1900. THIS ROW ONCE SAID «HER MARRIAGE IS OUT OF REACH». It was in a volume nobody had opened, four years before the window this archive had drawn for itself.

name: Francesco Antonio Arena
bornNote: Act 186 of 1819. Act 228 of 1861 makes him 42 on 23 December 1861 -- forty-two years and one month. The fit is exact.
source: Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186; Nati 1860 atto 45; Nati 1861 atto 228
note: ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE, which puts Rocco Arena under Orazio Arena instead. He and Serafina Arlotta have a son Giuseppe on 5 March 1860 and a son Rocco on 20 December 1861 -- exactly the sibling pair the tree assigns to Orazio.

name: Serafina Arlotta
bornNote: Act 2 of 1830. Twenty at her marriage on 7 February 1851 -- exact. Act 228 of 1861 makes her 28, which is three years adrift; she was 31.
source: Scilla, Nati 1830 atto 2; Matrimoni 1851 atto 13; Nati 1861 atto 228
note: ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. Her parents are now confirmed twice over: Giovanni Arlotta, marinaro, and Maria Costa.

name: Filippo Arena (the younger)
bornNote: Act 48 of 1852.
source: Scilla, Nati 1852, atto 48
note: Rocco Arena's eldest brother, named for their grandfather Filippo. Not in the family tree.

name: Domenica Arena
bornNote: ACT 53 of 1853 -- not act 2, which is a Tavola row number. Born at twelve o'clock on 24 March 1853 in her parents' own house and declared the same afternoon by her father.
source: Scilla, Nati 1853 atto 53, read in the original
note: ROCCO ARENA'S SISTER, NOT HIS BROTHER -- and this archive carried her as a son for weeks. The act says «una FEMINA», then «di dare alla FANCIULLA il nome di DOMENICA», and the baptism column names DOMENICA ARENA. Three statements in one act, none ambiguous. Her father is written out in full as FRANCESCANTONIO ARENA, thirty-two, MARINARO -- exact for a birth on 25 November 1819 -- and her mother SERAFINA ARLOTTA, twenty-two, exact for 13 June 1830. Not in the family tree. IT ALSO REMOVES A MYSTERY: a daughter who married leaves the Arena surname, so «Domenico Arena disappears after 1853» was never a disappearance.

name: Teresa Arena
bornNote: Act 6 of 1853.
source: Scilla, Nati 1853, atto 6
note: Orazio Arena's earliest known child. Not in the family tree -- which gives Orazio only the two children who turn out to be Francesco Antonio's.

name: Giovanni Arena (b. 1854)
bornNote: Scilla, act 76 of 1854, at nine in the morning, in his parents' house. NOT 20 April, and not the son of a Rosa Arlotta -- the annual Tavola is wrong on both counts and the act is right.
source: Scilla, Nati 1854, atto 76
note: ROCCO ARENA'S ELDER BROTHER. His birth act names his father ANTONIO ARENA, thirty-four -- Francesco Antonio, born 25 November 1819, is exactly thirty-four in April 1854 -- and his mother SERAFINA ARLOTTA, and it was declared by his maternal grandfather GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, who gave the boy his own name. This is the Giovanni Arena who sails in 1899 to join 'brother Rocco' and enters six-year-old Anna as his NIECE. HE IS IN THE FAMILY TREE, and this archive said for a time that he was not: the tree's Giovanni Arena, husband of Concetta Russo, IS this man, dated 1870 there and born in fact on 30 April 1854. What the act adds is sixteen years and two parents, not a person.

name: Giovanni Arlotta
bornNote: TWENTY-EIGHT at his own marriage on 30 August 1828. His daughter's birth act of 1830 makes him forty and his grandson's of 1854 makes him seventy-five -- three of his own declarations, twenty-one years apart. The marriage act is preferred: it is the one where age carried legal weight and it names his parents.
source: Scilla, Nati 1854 atto 76; Matrimoni 1851 atto 13; Nati 1830 atto 2; Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28
note: Serafina Arlotta's father, so Rocco Arena's maternal grandfather. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. A sailor. NOW IN THREE ACTS AND DATED: the marriage act of 1851, his daughter's birth act of 1830, and the birth act of 1854 in which he appears IN PERSON, aged seventy-five, to declare his grandson -- and which names HIS OWN FATHER, Domenico.

name: Maria Costa
bornNote: TWENTY-SIX at her marriage on 30 August 1828, with both her parents standing beside her and giving formal consent. CORRECTED THE SAME DAY IT WAS FIRST WRITTEN: her daughter's birth act of 1830 makes her twenty-three, which this archive entered as «c. 1807» that morning. Her own marriage act outranks her husband's statement at a registration desk.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1851 atto 13; Nati 1830 atto 2; Scilla, Nati 1830 atto 89 read in the processetti of 1851; Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28
note: Giovanni Arlotta's wife. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. NOTE THE SURNAME: she is the SECOND Costa in this generation -- Filippo Arena's wife is Domenica Costa -- and their great-grandson Rocco married a THIRD, Generosa Costa. A Lorenzo Costa was also lodging with Rocco in New York in 1900. CONFIRMED TWICE, by the 1851 marriage act and the 1830 birth act.

name: Gaetano Bonanno
bornNote: AGED THIRTY-SIX at his daughter Leonarda's birth in November 1843, so born about 1807. Piedimonte Etneo.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1843 atto 101; Matrimoni 1871 atto 14; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
note: Leonarda Bonanno's father. The archive had only the bare first name 'Gaetano', from a marriage proclamation of 1910; he is now in two registers with his surname, his trade and his age. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871: «figlia del VIVENTE GAETANO, professione bracciante, residente anche ivi», in his daughter Leonarda's publication certificate. Aged about sixty-four and still at Piedimonte.

name: Anna Cavallaro
bornNote: AGED THIRTY-EIGHT at Leonarda's birth in November 1843, so born about 1805.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1843 atto 101; Matrimoni 1871 atto 14; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
note: Gaetano Bonanno's wife, named in the register. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE -- and mind the namesake: the tree does hold an Anna Cavallaro, but she is the daughter of a Luciano Cavallaro BORN IN 1945 and has nothing to do with this woman, who was having children in the 1830s. Two different people, a century and a half apart. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871: «e della VIVENTE ANNA CAVALLARO, professione industriosa, residente anche ivi». First record of her trade, and a proof of life twenty-eight years after Leonarda's birth.

name: Domenico Arlotta
bornNote: Not sought. Scilla's civil registration begins in 1809, so his birth is pre-civil and would be a parish record.
source: Scilla, Nati 1854, atto 76
note: THE DEEPEST PERSON THIS ARCHIVE HAS REACHED ON THE CALABRIAN SIDE. Named only as 'il fu Domenico' in his son Giovanni Arlotta's own words, in the birth act of his great-grandson Giovanni Arena, 30 April 1854. A great-great-great-great-great-grandfather of Mia and Rocco. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. TIGHTENED BY TWENTY-SIX YEARS: he is «FU Domenico Arlotta» in his son's marriage act of 30 AUGUST 1828, so dead before then, not merely before April 1854. AND HE HAS A WIFE NOW: ANNA BARBARO, who was alive at that wedding.

name: Concetta Russo
bornNote: Aged TWENTY-SIX at her marriage in October 1885, so born about 1859. Scilla.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1885, atto 86
note: GIOVANNI ARENA'S WIFE. IN THE FAMILY TREE, which gives her no dates and no parents; the register gives both. Her age of thirty-three in her son Giuseppe's birth act of October 1892 puts her birth about 1859, and the same act names her parents LEONARDO RUSSO and ANGELA BAGNATO -- and those two are genuinely absent from the tree.

name: Leonardo Russo
bornNote: Not sought.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1885, atto 86
note: Concetta Russo's father, living at Scilla in 1885. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Angela Bagnato
bornNote: Not sought.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1885, atto 86
note: Concetta Russo's mother, living at Scilla in 1885. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Maria Martello
bornNote: Aged TWENTY-FOUR at her marriage in September 1885.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1885, atto 73
note: Giuseppe Arena's wife -- Giuseppe being Rocco Arena's brother, born 5 March 1860. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. Her father PAOLO MARTELLO was already RESIDENT IN AMERICA in 1885.

name: Anna Arlotta
bornNote: Not yet sought.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1888, atto 63
note: Generosa Costa's mother, named for the first time. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. AND NOTE THE SURNAME: Rocco Arena's mother is Serafina ARLOTTA and his wife's mother is Anna ARLOTTA. Whether they were sisters has not been tested, but if they were, Rocco and Generosa were first cousins.

name: Fortunato Arena
bornNote: Ten days old when he died on 1 October 1891, so born about the 21st of September. Via Grotte 70, Scilla.
source: Scilla, Morti 1891, atto 134
note: A son of ROCCO ARENA'S BROTHER Giovanni, dead at ten days. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. His death act fixes the household at VIA GROTTE -- the same street where his brother Giuseppe would be born thirteen months later, at number 75 -- and calls his father a PESCATORE, as Giuseppe's birth act does.

name: Antonio Costa
bornNote: AGED FORTY-EIGHT at his daughter Generosa's banns in November 1888, so born about 1840.
source: Scilla, Pubblicazioni 1888 no. 63; Matrimoni 1888 atto 63
note: Generosa Costa's father, now dated and with a trade. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Maria Donato
bornNote: Twenty-eight months old when she died on 16 February 1891, so born about October 1888. Via Grotte 21, Scilla.
source: Scilla, Morti 1891, atto 22
note: A daughter of MICHELE DONATO and MARIA SOFI, and a sister of Nunziata Donato, dead at two years and four months. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. Her death act gives her father's trade -- PESCATORE -- and the family's address.

name: Francesco Giovanni Rocco Arena
bornNote: Ten months old when he died on 30 June 1898, so born about August 1897. Via Acquagrande 30, Scilla.
source: Scilla, Morti 1898, atto 91
note: A NEPHEW OF ROCCO ARENA -- son of his brother Giuseppe and Maria Martello -- dead at ten months. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. His three given names are his paternal grandfather and both his uncles: FRANCESCO for Francesco Antonio Arena, GIOVANNI and ROCCO for his father's brothers.

name: Domenico Donato
bornNote: EXACT, from his own birth act copied into his marriage bundle — Scilla, Nati 1816, atto 207, declared by his father the day he was born. It agrees to the day with the thirty-eight he is given at his son Michele's birth on 3 October 1855.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129); Matrimoni 1844 atto 20; Nati 1855 atto 163
note: MICHELE DONATO'S FATHER, and a great-great-grandfather of Mia and Rocco. A sailor, like the Arena men. HE IS IN THE FAMILY TREE as Michele's father and nothing more -- no dates, no trade, no parents. This archive claimed for a time that he was absent; that was wrong. What is new is everything else about him: born about 1817, MARINARO, and son of CANDELORO DONATO and MARIA PALADINO, who are absent.

name: Nunziata Sofi
bornNote: From her own birth act copied into her marriage bundle — Scilla, Nati 1818, atto 129. Agrees with the thirty-seven she is given at her son's birth in October 1855.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129)
note: MICHELE DONATO'S MOTHER. IN THE FAMILY TREE, under the fuller form ANNUNZIATA SOFI, with no dates and no parents. Her son married a SOFI in his turn -- Maria Sofi -- and named his daughter NUNZIATA for her. What the 1844 Tavola adds is her parents, PASQUALE SOFI and MARIA DE AMICO, who are absent.

name: Candeloro Donato
bornNote: THIRTY-THREE when he declared his son Domenico's birth on 18 December 1816, so born about 1783. The first age this archive has ever had for him.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129); Matrimoni 1845, atto 31
note: THE OLDEST DONATO, and now dated. A sailor, like his son and his grandson. He was alive when his son Michele married in August 1845 -- «FIGLIO DI Candeloro Donato», not «del fu» -- and alive the year before too: his son Domenico's marriage bundle of July 1844 runs to FIVE FOGLI and contains no death certificate for either father, which this series required when a parent had died. HE IS WHERE THE SCILLA LINE STOPS. His own marriage, and any birth of his own, fall before 1816 when Scilla's civil registration begins, and his son Michele was born at MESSINA about 1814 where registration does not begin until 1820. Everything earlier is a parish record.

name: Rocco Arlotta
bornNote: Aged twenty-two at his marriage in June 1900.
source: FindMyPast, United States Marriages; US census 1900
note: THE ARLOTTA IN ROCCO ARENA'S HOUSEHOLD in the Manhattan census of June 1900, now identified: he married ANTONIETTA TAVANI in Manhattan on 4 June that same month. His father was ANTONIO Arlotta -- NOT the Giovanni Arlotta who was Serafina's father -- so he is not her nephew; a cousin is likelier and is untested. He stayed in New York: a Rocco Arlotta baptises children at Our Lady of Loretto, the Arena's own parish, in 1905 and 1908. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Antonino Prostamo
died: 31 December 1837, at Pizzo, in the cholera
source: Briatico, Matrimoni 1849, atto 1 — Antenati an_ua87663
note: The fourth generation, carried as UNTESTED until 14 September 2026 and now documented four times over. A MARINARO like his father and his son. He died at two in the morning on the last night of 1837 and his death is entered in Pizzo's SEPARATE REGISTER OF CHOLERA DEATHS, atto 327 — which is why the ordinary Morti volumes do not hold him. IN THE FAMILY TREE as antonino-prostamo-1785, where he is dated 1785 and given Pasquale Prostamo and a «Caterina Di Meio» as parents; the Pizzo register calls that same wife CATERINA MAJO.

name: Caterina Cichello
bornNote: TWENTY-SIX at her marriage on 2 March 1824, and BORN AT ZAMBRONE — so born about 1798, which agrees with the about-1799 this archive already had from her daughter's marriage bundle.
source: Zambrone, Matrimoni 1824, atto 2; Briatico, Matrimoni 1849, atto 1
note: GIOVANNA VENTRICE'S MOTHER, and now with parents. She married GIUSEPPE VENTRICE at ZAMBRONE on 2 MARCH 1824, and the act names her «figlia DEL FU FRANCESCO e DELLA FU VITTORIA MOLLO» -- both already dead when she married at twenty-six. She was widowed in June 1831, eighteen years before she appears alive at Briatico in her daughter's marriage papers of 1849.

name: Caterina Majo
source: Pizzo, Morti 1829, atto 7 — Antenati an_ua37926878
note: Pasquale Prostamo's wife, named because he is recorded as her WIDOWER; dead by January 1829. The family tree has no wife for the third generation. THIS ARCHIVE FIRST PUBLISHED HER AS «CATERINA MUSO». That was a misreading: the surname is MAJO in the original register and in the chancery's own certified copy of 1849, compared side by side.

name: Maria Fragalà
source: Pizzo, Nati 1814, atto 285; Pizzo morti colerici 1837, atto 327; Briatico, Matrimoni 1849, atto 1
note: Twenty-seven when her son was born in April 1814, so born about 1787. WIDOWED BY THE CHOLERA on the last night of 1837 and still living at Pizzo in June 1849, when her son married eleven kilometres away at Briatico. SHE IS IN THE FAMILY TREE, dated 1789 and married to Antonino Prostamo; this archive said for a time that she was not in it at all, which was wrong and is corrected here. What the Briatico act of 1849 adds is her widowhood, her town and her age.

name: Domenico Ventrice
source: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40 — certified extract in Briatico, Matrimoni processetti 1849-1854
note: Giovanna Ventrice's paternal grandfather, and the reason his certificate is in her marriage bundle: the act says she produced «la fede di morte del padre e dell'avo paterno», and the bundle holds exactly two Ventrice deaths. Died at Zambrone on 13 January 1815 at twenty-three o'clock, a BRACCIALE, husband of ANNA FAMA, and son of the late PAOLO VENTRICE and the late ANNA PAPPA. HIS AGE IS AMBIGUOUS IN THE ONLY SURVIVING TEXT: the copyist writes «sposo di Anna Fama di anni cinquanta ... di anni cinquantotto, di professione bracciale». The fifty-eight sits with his trade and is taken as his, so born about 1757; the fifty is taken as his wife's. This archive first published him as fifty.

name: Anna Fama
source: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40; Briatico, Morti 1839, atto 12
note: Domenico Ventrice's wife and Giuseppe Ventrice's mother. Given as «di anni cinquanta» in her husband's death act of January 1815 — on the reading that the first of that act's two ages is hers.

name: Paolo Ventrice
source: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40 — certified extract in Briatico, Matrimoni processetti 1849-1854
note: The deepest name on the bride's side, reached because his son's death act calls him «il fu Paolo». Husband of ANNA PAPPA.

name: Anna Pappa
source: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40
note: Paolo Ventrice's wife, already dead when their son Domenico died in 1815.

name: Giuseppe Ventrice
bornNote: THIRTY-FOUR at his marriage on 2 March 1824, so born about 1790 -- AND BORN AT S. COSTANTINO, not Zambrone, which is the first birthplace this archive has had for him. HIS TWO DECLARED AGES DISAGREE: thirty-four in March 1824 gives 1790, and thirty-three in June 1828 gives 1795. Both are his own statements. The earlier one is preferred here only because it is the earlier one.
source: Zambrone, Matrimoni 1824, atto 2; Briatico, Nati 1828; Briatico, Morti 1831, atto 12
note: Giovanna's father, and he died TWO DAYS BEFORE HER THIRD BIRTHDAY. Act 12 of Briatico Morti 1831, read in the original: dead at two in the morning on 21 June 1831 in his own house, «di anni TRENTA», declared by Giacomo Comerci, a miller, and Rosario Zungri, a bracciale. THE YEAR CORRECTS THIS ARCHIVE: the certified copy in the marriage bundle was read as 1839 and published that way; the original says 1831 and the rest of the 1839 register agrees it cannot be. HIS AGE IS STILL IN DISPUTE — thirty at death (born c. 1801) against the thirty-three he gave for HIMSELF when he registered Giovanna's birth in June 1828 (born c. 1795). The archive carries his own declaration and keeps the other on the record. HE MARRIED AT ZAMBRONE ON 2 MARCH 1824, a contadino of thirty-four born at S. COSTANTINO, and the act calls him «figlio DEL FU DOMENICO e DELLA FU ANNA MAROPOLI» -- so BOTH HIS PARENTS WERE DEAD by then, which dates his mother's death for the first time. On the surname MAROPOLI against this archive's ANNA FAMA, see the corrections page.

name: Francesco Crupi
source: Queensland death registrations 1973/B/38514, 1961/B/45635, 1982/52783, 1989/57278
note: ANGELA CRUPI'S FATHER. Named only because his children's Queensland death registrations name him -- and as of today there are FOUR of them, not one. Angela (d. 1973), PIETRO (d. 1961), ANTONINO (d. 1982) and MARIO (d. 1989) all register the same two parents, FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO. A whole Sicilian sibling group in Brisbane, of which this archive knew one. Not in the family tree.

name: Maria Vecchio
source: Queensland death registrations 1973/B/38514, 1961/B/45635, 1982/52783, 1989/57278
note: ANGELA CRUPI'S MOTHER, and named in FOUR of her children's Queensland death registrations -- Angela's, Pietro's, Antonino's and Mario's. Not in the family tree.

name: Candeloro Donato (b. 1847)
bornNote: Aged twenty-seven at his marriage on 11 December 1874. Scilla.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1874, atto 62
note: MICHELE DONATO'S ELDER BROTHER, and named for the grandfather who has his own row above, and new to this archive. Married DOMENICA ROMANO, 21, a spinner, at Scilla on 11 December 1874. He was a sailor like his father, and unmarried before it. His existence is what the naming custom predicted: Domenico Donato was «figlio di Candeloro», so his first son should be a Candeloro, and here he is.

name: Domenica Romano
bornNote: Aged twenty-one at her marriage in December 1874. Scilla.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1874, atto 62
note: Candeloro Donato's wife. Not in the family tree.

name: Marta Paladino
bornNote: THIRTY when her son Domenico was born in December 1816.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129); Matrimoni 1844, Tavola entry 17; Matrimoni 1845, atto 31
note: CANDELORO DONATO'S WIFE. HER GIVEN NAME IS IN DISPUTE AND THE DISPUTE IS WORTH KEEPING. Her son's birth act of 18 December 1816, written while she was in the next room, reads «e da MAR-TA PALADINO, di anni trenta, sua moglie legittima» -- the name broken across a line, and the second line beginning plainly «ta». The 1844 marriage Tavola calls her «Paladino MARIA». The act is contemporaneous and primary and the Tavola is an index made up at the year's end, and THIS VERY INDEX SERIES HAS ALREADY BEEN CAUGHT GIVING A MOTHER THE WRONG NAME -- the 1854 Tavola calls Serafina Arlotta «Rosa», and that error briefly made a brother into a cousin. Against that: the same 1844 Tavola gets the OTHER mother in the same entry exactly right, «de Amico Maria», as her own daughter's birth act confirms. So the index is not uniformly careless. MARTA is published here because the act says it; MARIA is recorded because the index says it. Another child of Candeloro in the Scilla births of 1810-1830 would settle it.

name: Pasquale Sofi
bornNote: THIRTY-EIGHT when he declared his daughter Nunziata's birth in November 1818.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129)
note: NUNZIATA SOFI'S FATHER, and a sailor like the Donato men he married into. Alive in July 1844: his daughter's marriage bundle holds no death certificate for him. Not in the family tree.

name: Maria de Amico
bornNote: TWENTY-FIVE when her daughter Nunziata was born in November 1818.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129); Matrimoni 1844, Tavola entry 17
note: Nunziata Sofi's mother. Not in the family tree. HER NAME IS CONFIRMED TWICE, by her daughter's birth act of 1818 and by the 1844 Tavola independently, which is why the Tavola's reading of the OTHER mother in the same entry is a question rather than a verdict -- see [[Marta Paladino]]. NOTE A COINCIDENCE, NOT A JOIN: the Michele Donato of act 31 of 1845 married an ANGELA DE AMICO. De Amico is common at Scilla and nothing yet connects the two women.

name: Michele Donato (b. Messina, c. 1814)
bornNote: Thirty-one at his marriage in August 1845, and the act says NATO IN MESSINA — the only member of this family so far recorded as born across the strait, in Sicily rather than Calabria.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1845, atto 31
note: DOMENICO DONATO'S ELDER BROTHER, and NOT THE MICHELE DONATO OF THIS ARCHIVE'S SPINE. Two men of the name stand three feet apart in these records: this one, born about 1814 at Messina, and his nephew born at Scilla on 3 October 1855 and named for him. Keep them apart. His act is what dates the grandfather — «FIGLIO DI Candeloro Donato», not «del fu», so CANDELORO WAS STILL ALIVE in August 1845 — and it is his mother's surname, PALADINO, that the 1844 Tavola then matched to make the brothers brothers.

name: Angela de Amico
bornNote: Thirty-two at her marriage in August 1845.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1845, atto 31
note: Michele Donato of Messina's wife. Not in the family tree. A COINCIDENCE AND NOT A JOIN: her husband's brother Domenico had married a Sofi whose own mother was a MARIA DE AMICO the year before. De Amico is common at Scilla and nothing yet connects the two women — but two de Amico women marrying into one Donato household in successive years is worth a look when the Scilla births of the 1810s are read.

name: Francesco Cichello
bornNote: Not yet sought. Zambrone's registers begin in 1811, so unless he outlived that he is pre-civil.
source: Zambrone, Matrimoni 1824, atto 2

name: Giuseppe Polistena

DATED AND GIVEN A TRADE: thirty-eight and a MARINARO in December 1836. That sets the Polistena beside the Arena and the Arlotta as another Scilla sailing family, and it is the first fact about him that is not a name on his son's death act. AND A DEATH BOUND AT LAST: «il FU Giuseppe» and «la FU Anna Pontillo» in their son Camillo Antonio's marriage act of 23 JANUARY 1881, each «residente in vita in Scilla». Both were alive at their daughter Fortunata's birth in January 1840 and dead by January 1881. A THIRD AGE, AND IT DOES NOT AGREE: he is FIFTY in September 1844 (Nati 1844 atto 137), against thirty-eight in December 1836 and thirty-four in December 1833. Births of 1794, 1798 and 1799. name: Orazio Arena (b. c. 1751)
bornNote: SEVENTY-NINE at his death on 12 July 1830 -- his own death act. This archive had inferred «about 1770» by working back from his sons and assuming a young father; he was about forty-two when Filippo was born.

note: THE TOP OF THE ARENA SPINE UNTIL THIS AFTERNOON, AND NOW NOT. He is a MARINARO in every record that gives him a trade, and the sea runs FIVE generations through him: his father Filippo, himself, his son Filippo, his grandson Francesco Antonio, his great-grandson Rocco. He stood at three of his sons' weddings -- Filippo's in 1815, Giuseppe's in 1821, Antonio's in 1828 -- and died at six in the morning on 12 July 1830, in his own house, with two young kinsmen to declare it. HIS OWN DEATH ACT NAMES HIS PARENTS: «figlio del fu FILIPPO ARENA e della fu SANTA UNGARO». Not in the family tree. AND THE NAMESAKE IS STILL A TRAP: the tree holds an «Orazio Arena» of generation six, father of Teresa Arena, the man it wrongly hangs Rocco Arena under. TWO DIFFERENT MEN, two generations apart.

name: Litteria Morabito
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore a parish record.

note: FILIPPO ARENA'S MOTHER, wife of Orazio Arena (b. c. 1751). Present in person at her son's marriage on 12 November 1815 and giving her consent with her husband. THE NAME IS LITTERIA, AND THIS ARCHIVE READ IT WRONG FOR AN AFTERNOON: the civil act's hand gives something like «Setteria», but her son's BAPTISM EXTRACT, copied into the marriage bundle in Latin by the parish economo on 26 May 1815, writes «ex Horatio Arena et LITTERIA MORABITO coniugibus». Litteria is a real and common name on this coast -- from the Madonna della Lettera, patroness of Messina, across the strait -- and «Setteria» is not. The clearer document wins. Not in the family tree. SHE OUTLIVED HIM: Orazio died 12 July 1830 and she is named without «fu» in the 1838 marriage Tavola, so she was still alive on 4 September 1838, a widow of eight years.

source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1845 atto 64; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
note: THE TOP OF THE SICILIAN SPINE, AND HE HAS BEEN FILED ON THE WRONG MAN. His son's birth act names him in his own words; his son is entered as «Rosario Mazza DI MARIANO» in the 1873 birth of Salvatore and again in the 1871 marriage. THE NAMESAKE TRAP, AND THIS ARCHIVE WALKED INTO IT: the family tree holds a «Mariano Mazza» who is the son of the ORAZIO MAZZA BORN 1883, himself a son of Rosario -- a twentieth-century man who cannot have fathered a boy in 1845. The 1845 record was attached to that slug and sat on his person page until 20 September. He is filed here as «Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809)» so no parent link can ever resolve to the wrong one. Not in the family tree. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871, AND THE DOCUMENT SAYS SO IN A PRINTED FIELD. The publication certificate for his son Rosario's marriage reads «figlio del VIVENTE MARIANO, professione bracciante, residente anche ivi» -- not the absence of a «fu» but the positive word, written into a form that has a blank for exactly this. He was about sixty-two, still a bracciante, still living at Piedimonte Etneo. TWENTY-SIX YEARS AFTER his own appearance at the comune house to declare Rosario's birth, and the second document in which he speaks for himself rather than being named by a descendant.

name: Maria Catalano
bornNote: THIRTY-SIX at her son Rosario's birth in June 1845, the same age as her husband.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1845 atto 64; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
note: ROSARIO MAZZA'S MOTHER, named in his birth act of 2 June 1845 and nowhere in the family tree. The parish of the CHIESA MAGGIORE returned the baptism notice the same day. She and Mariano were both thirty-six, so both born about 1809 -- which puts their marriage in the window the Piedimonte MATRIMONI PROCESSETTI cover from 1841, a series this archive has never opened. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871: «e della VIVENTE MARIA CATALANO, professione industriosa, residente anche ivi». The same certificate that gives her husband. It is also the first record of her TRADE -- industriosa, the word these registers use for a woman doing piecework at home.

name: Rosario Mazza
bornNote: Act 64 of 1845: born at eleven in the morning and declared the same day. The tree says 1850; his death act of 1924 makes him seventy-nine, which agrees with the register and not with the tree.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1845 atto 64; Matrimoni 1871 atto 14; Italy, Catania -- death 15 November 1924
note: HE IS IN THE FAMILY TREE; HIS PARENTS ARE NOT. This row exists only to carry the join: it anchors MARIANO MAZZA and MARIA CATALANO, both named in his own birth act, onto the export person the charts draw. Without it the chart closed his line with «Before Piedimonte Etneo, 1850» -- a card that reported the tree's silence and read as though the registers were silent too. They are not. He is the top of the Sicilian spine in the export; the two people above him are documented and the chart now draws them.

name: Mariano Mazza (b. 1872)
bornNote: Act 32 of 1872: born at ten in the evening of 12 February and declared at noon the next day by his father in person.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1872 atto 32
note: SALVATORE MAZZA'S ELDER BROTHER, AND THE NAMING CUSTOM CALLED HIM. Rosario Mazza's first son is named for ROSARIO'S OWN FATHER -- exactly what the custom predicts -- which is a third independent pointer at Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809) after the 1845 birth act and the «di Mariano» patronymic. Born in CONTRADA SAN BASILIO, the same lane the family is in when Salvatore is born eleven months later. ELEVEN MONTHS IS TIGHT: Salvatore was born 5 January 1873, so either this boy died in infancy or the two births are ten and a half months apart. Not in the family tree, and his death has not been sought. NOTE THE NAME: there are now THREE Mariano Mazza in this archive -- this baby, his grandfather (b. c. 1809), and the twentieth-century man in the family tree who is a son of the Orazio born 1883. All three are TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE twice over -- this baby of 1872, his grandfather born about 1809, and the tree's twentieth-century namesake -- and they are filed apart on purpose so that no father= in this file can resolve to the wrong one.

name: Gaetano Mazza
bornNote: Act 66 of 1880: born at half past four in the afternoon of 5 May and declared at a quarter past ten four days later by his father in person.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1880 atto 66
note: ANOTHER SON OF ROSARIO AND LEONARDA, AND THE NAMING CUSTOM CALLED HIM TOO. «Mazza Rosario, di anni trentadue, bracciante» declared him, born to «BONANNO LEONARDA, industriosa, sua moglie» in VIA S. BASILIO -- the same lane as his brother Mariano eight years earlier, and the mother's surname is given in full, which is what tells this household apart from the other Rosario-and-Leonarda in the town. GAETANO is the name the Sicilian custom gives after the MOTHER'S FATHER, and Leonarda's father is GAETANO BONANNO, named as such in the 1872 and 1873 acts. Witnesses Dimauro Salvatore, twenty-two, and Zappala Sebastiano, twenty-four. Not in the family tree, and his death has not been sought.

name: Domenico Arena (barbiere, b. c. 1743)
bornNote: SEVENTY at his son Diego's marriage on 12 August 1813, standing beside him and consenting -- so born about 1743, EARLIER THAN ANY OTHER ARENA IN THIS ARCHIVE.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1813 atto 21
note: AN ARENA HOUSEHOLD AT SCILLA WITH NO ESTABLISHED CONNECTION TO THIS FAMILY, and it is recorded here as exactly that. He is a BARBER where the spine is four generations of sailors, and the only Arena this archive has who was alive in the 1740s. His wife is ANNA MELIDONI and his eldest son DIEGO ARENA, sartore, married Maria Giuseppa Pontillo in 1813. HE IS NOT CLAIMED AS ORAZIO ARENA'S FATHER, and the temptation to claim him is the reason this note exists: Scilla has more than one Arena family, and TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE sharing a surname in one small town is how this archive nearly hung a birth act on the wrong Mariano Mazza a week ago. What would settle it is Orazio Arena's own marriage, which is pre-1809 and parish.

name: Anna Melidoni
bornNote: FIFTY-FOUR at her son Diego's marriage in August 1813.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1813 atto 21
note: Wife of Domenico Arena (barbiere, b. c. 1743), «domiciliante in casa di suo marito», present at her son's marriage and consenting with him. Like her husband she belongs to an Arena household this archive cannot yet connect to its own -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Arena of the spine until something says otherwise.

name: Diego Arena
bornNote: THIRTY-SEVEN at his marriage on 12 August 1813.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1813 atto 21
note: Married MARIA GIUSEPPA PONTILLO, sixteen, daughter of Giovanni Pontillo, forty-two, commerciante, and Diana Idone, at Scilla on 12 August 1813; the banns were published at CAMPO as well as Scilla. A TAILOR, in a family of barbers, and no established connection to the Arena of this archive's spine -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE until a record says otherwise. NOTE THE BRIDE'S SURNAMES: Pontillo and Idone both appear elsewhere in this archive, in the Polistena and Costa households. That is a coincidence of common Scilla names and is written down as one.

name: Carlo Arena
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1812, Tavola annuale, atto 10
note: A THIRD ARENA FATHER AT SCILLA IN THE SAME DECADE AS ORAZIO, and no connection to him is claimed. His daughter GIOVANNA ARENA married Giovanni La Mussa on 6 January 1812; the Tavola names her parents as «Carlo, ed Eugenia Ateja». TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Arena of this archive's spine until a record says otherwise -- the napoleonic marriage years hold Domenico the barber, Carlo, and Orazio, three Arena fathers with nothing between them.

name: Antonia Arena
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1811 atto 22; Matrimoni 1812 atto 1
note: DEAD BEFORE FEBRUARY 1811, and dated by two indexes rather than by an act. She is «fu Antonia Arena», wife of DOMENICO FALCOMATA, in the 1811 Tavola when her daughter GIUSEPPA FALCOMATA marries Tomaso Spoliti of Bagnara, and again in the 1812 Tavola when her daughter NUNZIATA FALCOMATA marries Angelo Porchese of Reggio. Both entries give the same parents, so the two brides are sisters and one household. No connection to this archive's Arena is claimed -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE until something says otherwise.

name: Giuseppe Arena (b. c. 1794)
bornNote: TWENTY-SEVEN on 7 November 1821, at his own solenne promessa -- so born about 1794.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1821 atto 29; Tavola annuale 1821
note: FILIPPO ARENA'S BROTHER, AND THE FIRST SIBLING THIS ARCHIVE HAS EVER FOUND FOR HIM. Same parents, same trade, same town: «figlio di ORAZIO ARENA, di professione MARINARO, e di LITTERIA MORABITO». He married MARIA TERESA POLISTINA at Scilla on 13 November 1821, the promessa taken six days earlier before Tommaso Cutelli, the same sindaco who married Filippo in 1815. THE AGES ARE TIGHT: Filippo was born 25 March 1793 and Giuseppe's age puts him in 1794, eight to twenty months later -- possible, and equally possible that one declared age is a year out, which is routine here. NOTE THE NAME: the family tree holds a GIUSEPPE ARENA born 1860, son of Francesco Antonio -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE two generations apart, and the later one is named for this one, which is what the naming custom predicts.

name: Maria Teresa Polistina
bornNote: TWENTY-ONE at her marriage on 13 November 1821, «nata in questo Comune».
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1821 atto 29; Tavola annuale 1821
note: GIUSEPPE ARENA'S WIFE, and an ARENA-POLISTINA marriage a century before the two surnames meet again in this family. Both her parents were dead by November 1821. NOTE WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this archive's Polistena line at Scilla is not connected to her, and Polistina is a common name in the town.

name: Raffaele Polistina
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1821 atto 29
note: «RAFAELE POLISTINA, DEFONTO» at his daughter Maria Teresa's promessa on 7 November 1821, and «fu Raffaele» in the Tavola -- so dead before that date. Nothing else is known of him.

name: Vittoria Morabito
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1821, Tavola annuale; atto 29
note: MARIA TERESA POLISTINA'S MOTHER, dead before November 1821. AND THE ARCHIVE'S TWO WITNESSES DISAGREE ABOUT HER NAME: the annual Tavola writes «Vittoria Morabito» and the act itself appears to write «Litteria Morabito, defonta» -- which is the name of the GROOM'S living mother. Two women of the name, or a clerk's eye slipping up a line. The Tavola is preferred here only because it does not repeat itself, and the doubt is recorded rather than hidden. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from Litteria Morabito either way: one was alive that day and one was not.

name: Antonio Arena (m. 1828)
bornNote: Not sought. His brothers are 1793 and about 1794, so he is probably later in the 1790s; the marriage act itself would give his age.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 26; Tavola annuale 1828
note: FILIPPO ARENA'S SECOND BROTHER, found the same way as the first: the annual Tavola names all four parents, and this one opens on «ARENA ANTONIO e DE LUCA SERAFINA -- ORAZIO, e MORABITO LETTERIA». He married SERAFINA DE LUCA at Scilla on 10 August 1828. So Orazio Arena and Litteria Morabito had at least three sons: Filippo (b. 1793, m. 1815), Giuseppe (b. c. 1794, m. 1821) and Antonio (m. 1828). THE NAME NEEDS ITS BRACKET: this archive holds two Antonio Arena born at New York in 1896 and 1902, and the family tree holds more -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE, a century apart, and this row is the Scilla one.

name: Serafina de Luca
bornNote: Not sought; her marriage act would give her age.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1828, Tavola annuale, entry 1
note: ANTONIO ARENA'S WIFE, married at Scilla on 10 August 1828. Her father FILIPPO DE LUCA was already dead -- «fu Filippo» -- and her mother ANNA ALFONZETTO was living. NOTE THE SURNAME, AND NOTE THAT NOTHING IS CLAIMED FROM IT: Alfonzetto is the same name as MARTA ALFONZETTI, Domenica Costa's mother, who was alive at Scilla in 1815. Two Alfonzetti women in one family's circle is what a small town looks like, not a connection.

name: Domenico Arena (m. 1838)
bornNote: Not sought. His brothers run 1793 to about 1800, so probably the same decade; the marriage act would give his age.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1838 atto 20; Tavola annuale 1838
note: FILIPPO ARENA'S THIRD BROTHER. The 1838 Tavola opens on him: «ARENA DOMENICO e POLISTINA TERESA -- FU ORAZIO, e Lett.a Morabito». He married TERESA POLISTINA at Scilla on 4 September 1838. HE IS ALSO THE MAN WHO DATES HIS FATHER'S DEATH: the «fu» before Orazio is the only one in any Arena entry this archive has read, and it brackets Orazio's death to the ten years after August 1828. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Domenico Arena, barbiere, born about 1743 who appears in the 1813 marriage of Diego Arena -- that one is two generations up and no connection is claimed.

name: Teresa Polistina
bornNote: Not sought.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1838, Tavola annuale, entry 1
note: DOMENICO ARENA'S WIFE, married 4 September 1838, and the SECOND Polistina daughter of «fu Raffaele e Letteria Morabito» to marry a son of Orazio Arena -- MARIA TERESA POLISTINA married his brother GIUSEPPE in 1821. EITHER TWO SISTERS MARRIED TWO BROTHERS, OR ONE WIDOW MARRIED HER BROTHER-IN-LAW. Nothing read so far settles it; the Scilla death registers of 1821-1838 would. Recorded as two people because the two Tavole give two different given names, and merging them would be a guess.

name: Santo Arena
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1833, Tavola annuale; Matrimoni 1821, Tavola annuale
note: THE FATHER OF TWO ARENA GROOMS AND NOT OURS. His son ROCCO married Domenica Costa on 10 June 1821 and his son FRANCESCO married Concetta Palermo on 13 December 1833; both entries give the mother as VITTORIA FIORENZA, which is what makes them brothers. The 1833 entry writes «fu Santo», so he was dead by then; the 1821 entry's father's name is cut by the page edge and this is what supplies it. NO CONNECTION TO ORAZIO ARENA IS CLAIMED -- Scilla holds at least seven Arena households in this period.

name: Filippo Arena (the elder, d. before 1830)
bornNote: Not sought; he belongs to the 1720s and is pre-civil.
source: Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64
note: GENERATION NINE. «FIGLIO DEL FU FILIPPO ARENA e della fu SANTA UNGARO» -- the death act of his son ORAZIO, 12 July 1830. The «fu» dates him dead before that day; his son was born about 1751, so he belongs to the 1720s and everything about him is pre-civil and parish. AND HE EXPLAINS A NAME: Orazio's first son, born 25 March 1793, is FILIPPO -- the Sicilian and Calabrian custom giving the first son his father's father. This archive used the custom to RANK candidates for four months and never once to identify one; here the act confirms it after the fact, which is the only way round that is safe. THERE ARE NOW THREE FILIPPO ARENA in this archive: this one, his grandson born 1793, and that man's grandson born 1852. All three are filed apart on purpose.

name: Santa Ungaro
bornNote: Not sought; 1720s, and pre-civil.
source: Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64
note: ORAZIO ARENA'S MOTHER, and the second person of generation nine on this side. «Della FU Santa Ungaro» in her son's death act of July 1830, so dead before then. UNGARO is a surname new to this archive. Nothing else is known of her and nothing else is likely to be: Scilla's civil registers begin in 1809, fifty-eight years after her son was born.

name: Diego Arena (b. c. 1808)
bornNote: TWENTY-TWO when he declared his relative's death on 12 July 1830.
source: Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64
note: ONE OF THE TWO MEN WHO DECLARED ORAZIO ARENA'S DEATH, and the act calls him «NIPOTE DEL DEFONTO» -- which in Italian is nephew OR grandson and this archive will not choose for it. A MARINARO at twenty-two, like the man he was burying. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Diego Arena, sartore, who was thirty-seven in 1813: that one was born about 1776. His exact place in the household is unresolved and the Scilla birth registers of 1808 would settle it.

name: Prospero Arena
bornNote: TWENTY-FIVE when he declared Orazio Arena's death on 12 July 1830.
source: Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64
note: THE SECOND DECLARANT AT ORAZIO ARENA'S DEATH, also «nipote del defonto» and also a MARINARO. Born about 1805, so too old to be a son of Filippo (m. 1815) or Giuseppe (m. 1821) -- which makes nephew more likely than grandson, and would mean ORAZIO HAD A BROTHER. Recorded as a question, not an answer.

name: Giuseppe Arena (d. 1925)
bornNote: Not sought. His parents married on 4 September 1838, so he belongs to the 1840s or later.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla deaths: «Giuseppe Arena, Morte: Scilla 27/03/1925, Padre Domenico, Madre Teresa Polistena, Coniuge Serafina Vita»
note: A CHILD OF FILIPPO ARENA'S BROTHER DOMENICO, and the first evidence that the 1838 marriage produced anyone. He died at Scilla on 27 March 1925, husband of SERAFINA VITA. THE ENTRY ALSO CONFIRMS TERESA POLISTINA INDEPENDENTLY: this archive had her only from the 1838 annual Tavola, and here she is again as a mother, eighty-seven years later, in a different series indexed by a different hand. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Giuseppe Arena born about 1794 who is Filippo's brother, and from the Giuseppe Arena born 1860 who is Rocco's -- three men of the name in three generations of one extended family, which is what the naming custom does to an archive.

name: Teresa Arena (d. 1943)
bornNote: Not sought.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla deaths: «Teresa Arena, Morte: Scilla 27/08/1943, Padre Giuseppe, Madre Serafina Vita, Coniuge Gaetano Cosentino»
note: GRANDDAUGHTER OF DOMENICO ARENA AND TERESA POLISTINA, and named for her grandmother exactly as the custom predicts. She died at Scilla on 27 August 1943, wife of GAETANO COSENTINO. Her line is a cousin branch of this archive's own: her great-grandfather ORAZIO ARENA is Filippo's father. NOTHING HERE JOINS HER TO THE SPINE beyond that shared great-grandfather, and nothing should.

name: Giovanni Nicotra (John)
bornNote: THIRTY-ONE at his marriage on 7 October 1872, so born about 1841. At MASCALI, not Piedimonte.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 (7 October 1872), read in the original
note: MARIA NICOTRA'S FATHER, and the man the Queensland death registration of 1963 calls «John Nicotra» and nothing else. Here he is in his own act: «sono comparsi GIOVANNI NICOTRA, di anni trentuno, di professione bracciante, DOMICILIATO E RESIDENTE A MASCALI, figlio di ROSARIO, di professione bracciante, e di VENERA MURABITO, contadina, domiciliati e residenti PURE IN MASCALI». HE IS NOT A PIEDIMONTE MAN. He married into the town and lived in the next one, which is why fourteen consecutive Piedimonte birth indexes produced no daughter of his.

name: Venera Cassaniti
bornNote: TWENTY-FOUR on 7 October 1872, so born about 1848 -- and Piedimonte Nati 1848 atto 45 is «CASSANITI VENERA», born the fourteenth. The two fit without strain.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 (7 October 1872), read in the original; Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1848 atto 45 (annual Tavola)
note: MARIA NICOTRA'S MOTHER, and the archive spent days unable to touch her because the Queensland registrar wrote CASSANETI, a spelling that exists nowhere in Italy. She is CASSANITI. «E VENERA CASSANITI, di anni ventiquattro, QUI domiciliata e residente, figlia del FU GAETANO, e di FU MARIA CURRENTI» -- both her parents already dead in October 1872, and she the one of the couple who belonged to Piedimonte.

name: Rosario Nicotra
bornNote: «di anni novanta circa» at death in April 1890.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20; Mascali, Nati 1873 atto 145; Mascali, Morti 1890 atto 35 — all read in the original
note: FOUND, 9 October 2026, in Mascali Morti 1890 atto 35. «è morto NICOTRA ROSARIO, di anni NOVANTA CIRCA, CONTADINO, residente in Mascali, NATO IN GIARRE, da fu SIMONE, e da fu MUSUMECI MARIANNA, MARITO DI MURABITO VENERA», died 4 April 1890 at contrada Montargi. After three documents he has a birthplace, a birth year, a trade, a death, two parents and his wife named beside him. He was BORN AT GIARRE about 1800 — which is very likely why his son Giovanni said «nato a Giarre» — and he had moved to Mascali by 1872. Three independent acts now name him: his son's marriage in 1872, his granddaughter's birth in 1873 where he is «di Rosario» and alive, and his own death.

name: Venera Murabito
bornNote: Not stated; alive in October 1872.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20; Mascali, Morti 1890 atto 35, read in the original
note: GIOVANNI NICOTRA'S MOTHER, of MASCALI, named without «fu» and so alive on 7 October 1872. A contadina. The tree's own household holds a daughter VENERA NICOTRA, and a first daughter is named for the paternal grandmother -- though her mother was a Venera too, so the custom points both ways here and is not evidence on its own. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE, like every person above generation four on this side. ALIVE ON 4 APRIL 1890. Her husband's death act calls him «MARITO di Murabito Venera» — marito, not vedovo, and that register writes «vedovo» for a widower on the same pages. So she outlived him, and her death act is the next document to find: it would give her age, her parents, and the Murabito household she came from.

name: Gaetano Cassaniti
bornNote: Not stated.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 (7 October 1872), read in the original; Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1848 atto 45 (annual Tavola)
note: VENERA CASSANITI'S FATHER, of Piedimonte Etneo, and DEAD BY OCTOBER 1872: his daughter's marriage act calls her «figlia del FU GAETANO». He is also the father named in her birth entry in the annual Tavola of Nati 1848, act 45, which is what ties the birth to the marriage. MIND THE NAMESAKE: Piedimonte held a GAETANO BONANNO and a GAETANO BONACCORSO at the same period, both braccianti, and this is a third Gaetano again.

name: Maria Currenti
bornNote: Not stated.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 (7 October 1872), read in the original
note: VENERA CASSANITI'S MOTHER, dead by October 1872 -- «e di FU MARIA CURRENTI». AND SHE CORRECTS A READING OF MY OWN MADE AN HOUR EARLIER: the 1848 annual Tavola band, read at 640 pixels, gave her as «Venuti Maria». The marriage act, read at full width, says CURRENTI. Same class of error as the Bonanno/Bonaccorso confusion in the same sweep, and the same remedy -- a name off a contact sheet is a hypothesis, not a reading.

name: Simone Nicotra
bornNote: Not stated.
source: Mascali, Morti 1890 atto 35 (4 April 1890), read in the original
note:
GENERATION SEVEN, AND THE OLDEST NICOTRA THIS ARCHIVE HAS REACHED on the line that leads to the children. Named in his son's death act: «NICOTRA ROSARIO ... nato in GIARRE, da fu SIMONE, e da fu MUSUMECI MARIANNA». Dead by April 1890, and since Rosario was born about 1800 at Giarre, Simone was fathering children there at the turn of the century — before Sicilian civil registration began in 1820, which is why no birth act for Rosario can exist.
A SIMONE NICOTRA IS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE. Giarre's very first register year, Nati 1820, holds two untitled Nicotra households and one of them is SIMONE NICOTRA x DADONE. A man fathering a child at Giarre in 1820 and a man fathering Rosario at Giarre about 1800 are entirely consistent, and the forename is uncommon. IT IS NOT JOINED. The 1820 act names a wife this one does not match, and a shared forename in one town is exactly the trap this archive has refused a dozen times. The test is Giarre's pre-1820 parish registers or a Mascali marriage act for Rosario and Venera.

name: Marianna Musumeci
bornNote: Not stated.
source: Mascali, Morti 1890 atto 35 (4 April 1890), read in the original
note: GENERATION SEVEN, Rosario Nicotra's mother, named in his death act of 1890 as «fu MUSUMECI MARIANNA» — dead by then. Musumeci is among the commonest surnames in both Giarre and Mascali, so she cannot be traced on the name alone; what she gives is the second half of a couple and a maiden surname to search.

name: Alfio Nicotra (of Rosa Pappalardo)
bornNote: From «d'anni settanta» in his death act; the word is cramped and SIXTY cannot be wholly excluded, which would give 1782.
source: Giarre, Morti 1842 atto 189, read in the original
note: «ALFIO NICOTRA D'ANNI SETTANTA, SPOSO DI ROSA PAPPALARDO, nato in Giarre, di professione BRACCIALE, FIGLIO DI FU GIUSEPPE e di FU LEONARDA PENNISI». He buried two grown children at Giarre — Isidoro in 1831 and Francesca in 1836, both «di Nicotra Alfio e Pappalardo Rosa» — and his son SALVADORE married at Riposto in 1844 and died at Mascali in 1848. HE IS NOT the Alfio Nicotra who died at Mascali in 1869: that man was born about 1796 and his mother was a CATERINA. Standing in Simone Nicotra's own generation in the same town and trade, he is a candidate brother and NOTHING ATTACHES HIM. Generation is inferred from birth year against SIMONE NICOTRA, who is gen 7 and born about 1776. NOBODY HERE IS ATTACHED TO THE TREE; the number places them in time, not in the descent.

name: Giuseppe Nicotra (of Leonarda Pennisi)
bornNote: Not stated; dead before December 1842.
source: Giarre, Morti 1842 atto 189, read in the original
note: Named as «FU GIUSEPPE» in his son Alfio's death act, so dead by December 1842. THE OLDEST NICOTRA GENERATION REACHED AT GIARRE BY A DEATH ACT. If Simone Nicotra is his son too, this is Simone's parentage — THAT IS NOT PROVED, and the Giarre Morti sweep of 1820-1860 holds no Giuseppe Nicotra as a decedent, so he probably died before civil registration began in 1820 and is parish-only. GIARRE HELD SEVERAL GIUSEPPE NICOTRAS and they must not be merged: a Giuseppe x Rosaria Misano, a D. Giuseppe x D. Gioachina Caltabiano, a Giuseppe x Carmela Coco, and the Giuseppe born about 1797 who married Rosa Cattabiano in 1820. Generation is inferred from birth year against SIMONE NICOTRA, who is gen 7 and born about 1776. NOBODY HERE IS ATTACHED TO THE TREE; the number places them in time, not in the descent.
